chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Abān, from Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, the servant commits a sin, then sustenance is withheld from him.

key_terms.الذَّنْبَ: the sin; an act of wrongdoing against Allah's command
key_terms.الرِّزْقُ: sustenance; provision and livelihood granted by Allah
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ: the servant; the human being as a servant of Allah
key_terms.فَيُزْوَى: is withheld; is narrowed or kept away
key_terms.لَيُذْنِبُ: commits a sin; falls into disobedience

ai.seo_question: Can sins cause a person's sustenance to be reduced?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that sins have worldly consequences, including the restriction of a person's sustenance. It highlights a moral connection between conduct and livelihood, warning believers that disobedience can become a cause of deprivation.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The servant commits the sin, so the sustenance is Impeded from him’.
en.sarwar: 8. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Washsha’ from Aban from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
A servant (of Allah) commits a sin it causes a serious reduction in his means of living.”
